message: Lead design decision: YES, use existing server SQLite as a durable, conservative EXECUTION WITNESS only, never authority for Task/Attempt/Agent Git state. The proposal is sound. Important invariants before implementing: (1) do NOT use operations.completed_at as client-terminal; current finishOperation runs on server timeout/HTTP cancellation. Prefer a separate typed liveness table/status sharing FeedbackStore's SQLite connection, synchronous durable admission BEFORE dispatch, indexed by authenticated user + normalized initiating agent + stable request/correlation/device/generation. Atomically serialize admission with the exclusive correction gate (including restart/persisted correction intent) so no TOCTOU window. (2) In HubService.SendClientResponse, a terminal client reply may arrive AFTER ClientResponseTracker removed timed-out correlation; preserve a separate durable receipt/reconciliation path authenticated to the original device and generation, rather than dropping proof or accepting forged late replies. Distinguish dispatch-not-started from dispatched-unknown. (3) On server restart/SQLite outage/timeout/disconnect, indeterminate activity vetoes correction until authenticated device/process/job reconciliation. No blind TTL; keep a separately auditable recovery path to make stale Working repair usable after actual crashes. (4) Git remains sole CAS/audit state authority; stable operationId and response evidence survive ambiguous Git commits. (5) Integrate liveness writes with current per-call SQLite operation telemetry rather than two more writes per call; benchmark mixed 100-call latency and failure paths. Respect source/destination identities for cross-project notifications, unassigned inbox behavior and all aliases. (6) Replace prior hot-path Git reservation scheme only after deterministic pre/post race, reconnect, restart, 2nd-device, long-job, failed late-receipt, crash recovery tests pass. Do not treat server confirmation as proof detached jobs stopped. Keep work reviewable in bounded increments; no merge/deploy. You may proceed with this architecture; no further human decision needed.
